name: Conspiracy Central
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading, cut to Hall of Femme's
design. Everything that makes it a Snapchat pack is Hall of Femme's
and is taken from the same two presets rather than restated: the
frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite that turns speech into report, the stated 40px, the twenty
characters to a line, the freeform text box, the drag, and now the
What makes it a different show is three decisions. The block is set
in Bebas Neue Cyrillic with picked words in Poppins; the colours are
black, a periwinkle, a mint and white, which the user pairs between
the type and the card; and a dark shade rises from the foot of the
frame, which the Gradient button switches. Each is argued where it
is stated. Where the block stands is NOT one of them - see
The id is kebab-case ASCII because it is also the folder name and the
key everything else refers to; the name is the brand.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: Where this show parts company with the pack it was cut from. Hall of
Femme sets its captions in two cuts of Telegraf on a hot pink card;
this one is set in Bebas Neue Cyrillic, with picked words in Poppins,
in four colours the user pairs per frame, on a card.
It used to be the one pack under the heading with no card and no
palette: Anton in near-white straight on the photograph, held off it
by a drop shadow, with picked words in near-black on a yellow box.
The show has since asked for four colours of its own, and offering
them for a ground as well as for the letters is a request for a card
- the panel palette cannot exist without one (see editor.paletteOf).
So it is on the card its siblings use, and what follows from that is
written once, in content/README.md, under 'A channel that set its
caption on the photograph may take the card back': the card is the
preset's, the shadow goes, and the yellow box goes with it, because a
box inside a card is a shape inside a shape.
One thing is unlike those nine. They kept the show's old colour first
in the list, as the swatch a user reaches for to undo a choice. This
show REPLACED its colours rather than adding to them - the near-white
and the near-black became true white and true black, and the yellow
is gone - so there is nothing old left to keep, and the list is the
four colours in the order they were asked for.
Uppercased, inherited from the preset, and this pack could not
sensibly turn it off: Bebas has no lower case of its own, so a
caption in Poppins' lower case would have its block in capitals and
its picked words not, and the highlight would be carrying a
difference nobody chose.

_comment_face: Bebas Neue Cyrillic - a different file from the Bebas Neue that
beauty-tipps is set in, with a family name of its own, and
content/faces/bebas-neue-cyrillic.json says why that name is what
keeps the two from being drawn as one another. noisy-dish is set
in this file too, cut to this pack's design.
A tall condensed display face whose capitals fill the em. On a
card it needs nothing else to hold it, which is the job Anton's
drop shadow was doing when the type lay on the photograph.
_comment_color: White, and the channel's own answer: what every frame is set in
until somebody presses a swatch, since a frame stores no colour
of its own until it is given one (see state.textColorFor).
True #FFFFFF, where the pack used to state #FEFEFD and argue for
the warmth in it. That argument was about white beside the yellow
box, and the show has asked for an absolute white and an absolute
black instead; with the yellow gone there is nothing left for a
warm white to be warm against.
It is also the colour of a picked word - see `highlight` - so
the whole caption is one colour until the highlight row is
pressed, and what separates a picked word is the face.
_comment_colors: Black, the periwinkle #7D7EF2, the mint #79FFB1 and white, in the
order the show gave them, offered for the letters and for the
card behind them - four buttons each in the title panel (see
The same four in both lists and in one order, which is what Hall
of Femme does and for its reason: the point is the PAIRING. White
on black is what the channel opens on; black on mint, black on
periwinkle and white on periwinkle are a button away.
Nothing stops the user setting black on black. The two lists are
independent because the pairing is the feature, and the user can
see the caption has gone and presses another swatch.
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block, as a row of
its own - see the note on `colors` in js/channels.js. Until that
row is pressed on a frame, picked words follow the block.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Poppins Regular, in the same white as the
rest of the block. The colour is stated and it is the block's, so
the recolour draws exactly what its neighbours are drawn in and
the FACE is the whole of the difference until the user gives the
picked words a colour of their own from the highlight row.
It is the opposite move to beauty-tipps, which sets a plain block
and picks words out in condensed Bebas. Here Bebas is the block,
and a picked word comes out wide, round and lighter than the
words either side of it - it changes the shape of the line and
not only its texture, which is what makes it read at a glance on
a phone. That the two faces set at one size come out at two
apparent sizes costs nothing here: the preset states `fontSize`,
so there is no per-line fit for the wider face to win (see the
note on two faces in content/README.md).
Colour mode, word scope and no shadow are the preset's and are
not restated. The box, its yellow fill and the shadow this pack
used to state for it belonged to type lying on the photograph;

_comment_panel: Black, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
Black because it is the first colour the show asked for and the
white type reads on it at once - the job the drop shadow used to
do letter by letter, given to the whole line instead.
_comment_layout: No `layout` of its own: the preset's block, stood on the foot of
the frame at its 120px margin, where every Snapchat caption
stands - nearly the full width, a stated 40px, twenty characters
to a line, `freeform`, all argued in the preset.
It used to be hung from the HEAD of the frame instead (vAlign

_comment_scrim: A shade thrown up from the foot of the frame to its middle, over
the photograph and under the card. The show asked for the Thumbnail
Maker's dark gradient turned on its side - from the bottom of the
picture towards the top - and this is that gradient, number for
number.
The backend's ramp (reframe_engine.apply_dark_gradient) darkens by
a peak of 0.65 at its edge and falls in a straight line to nothing
at half the frame. A black stop at alpha 0.65 is the same arithmetic
- black laid over a pixel at alpha a leaves it at (1 - a) of
itself, which is exactly the multiplier the backend applies - and
two stops make the same straight line, so heightRatio 0.5 and these
two stops are that ramp, measured from the floor instead of from
the side.
One thing it does not copy: the backend scales its peak by how
bright the part of the photograph it covers already is, between
0.35 and 0.85 (_adaptive_gradient_strength). A scrim is drawn on
the canvas from fixed stops and has no pixels to measure, so it
takes the 0.65 that adaptation was validated around.
Unlike laugh-society-snapchat's scrim it is not what holds the
caption legible - the card does that, standing in the shade at the
foot of the frame as a shadow behind it. It is part of the look
of the show, which is why it is offered at all on a carded pack and
why it arrives on (see `branding` below). It ends on a fully
transparent stop, so there is no line across the picture where it
stops; there is no way to aim it at an angle, and that is
deliberate - see `scrim` in js/channels.js.
_comment_branding: `gradient` is true, and on this channel it means the SCRIM above
rather than the backend's side gradient - the same thing it means on
laugh-society-snapchat. A channel with a scrim draws its own shade
on the canvas, the Gradient button switches it per frame with no
round trip, and the backend is never asked for its ramp as well
(see state.backendPresentation), so a still is not darkened twice,
in two directions, for one press.
On arrival because the shade is part of how this show looks rather
than an effect to go and find. The button turns it off for the frame
whose picture is already dark enough at the foot, or where the shade
lands across something that should stay lit.
